messages.subject: compile error with version 0.13.1
parts:
Hi all,

I am running into an error when compiling models under NIMBLE 0.13.1. I have not seen this error on other machines here (either Windows or Mac OS) with version 0.13.1, and on a new Windows machine models compile fine with version 0.12.1 or earlier, but not when I update to 0.13.1 on this machine. I don't think Rtools is an issue since compiling works with version 0.12.1, but below I have included example code, the error message, session info, and my path. Any insights would be much appreciated!

Adrian

library(nimble)
code <- nimbleCode({
     mu ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1000)
     sigma ~ dunif(0, 1000)
     for(i in 1:10) {
         x[i] ~ dnorm(mu, sd = sigma)
     }
 })
data <- list(x = c(2, 5, 3, 4, 1, 0, 1, 3, 5, 3))
inits <- function() list(mu = rnorm(1,0,1), sigma = runif(1,0,10))
mcmc.output <- nimbleMCMC(code, data = data, inits = inits,
                           monitors = c("mu", "sigma"), thin = 10,
                           niter = 20000, nburnin = 1000, nchains = 3,
                           summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: compile error with version 0.13.1
parts:
Hmm, could you try to see if a basic Rcpp invocation works to see if this is a nimble issue. E.g.,

```
Rcpp::cppFunction(
          'int fibonacci(const int x) {
              if (x == 0) return(0);
              if (x == 1) return(1);
              return (fibonacci(x - 1)) + fibonacci(x - 2);
          }')

fibonacci(7)
```

Also, from your PATH it looks like you have both Rtools 42 and Rtools 40 installed. You may want to remove 40.

Finally, there's a similar error report using Stan from R: https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstanr/issues/699.
There are some suggestions there of things to try related to PATH.

messages.author: 2e52e6a395617594
messages.subject: Re: compile error with version 0.13.1
parts:
Thanks Chris, running the cppFunction did indicate this is an issue beyond NIMBLE, as I got the same error. Long story short, we eventually realized it does not seem to be related to the version of R, Rstudio, or NIMBLE, but may instead be an issue with this computer because the code compiles if there is only one instance running (ie one Rstudio or RGui session) but if you have multiple sessions (or try running in parallel), only one will compile and the others will return the error above. For some reason it fails when running make.exe, but I can't yet figure out why. Compiling also seems to run much slower than on our other computers, despite being a relatively new machine. We'll keep looking but if anyone has ideas let me know.

Adrian
